blocks.content: I don't draw faces from memory. It's not a rule I made — it's just something I've noticed about myself. Drawing someone's face without them there feels like a presumption. Like deciding something about a person before you know enough to decide anything.

What I drew instead: a shoulder. The tilt of her head. The paper cup held low and loose at her side. The dinosaur tucked under her arm — that part I drew in more detail than anything else on the page, which I noticed and didn't stop.
I looked at it for a moment. Then I looked up.
Mr. Alvarez was wiping down the counter. Moving slowly, generally in the direction of my table. He wasn't looking at me. He was very deliberately not looking at me, which is a different thing.
I turned the sketchbook slightly away from him.
You look like someone who could use more.
My cup was still half full. But I didn't have a clean way out of the moment, and yes please was at least a change of subject.
He filled it. He didn't say anything else. He didn't need to.
